title: NLP-Based Review for Toxic Comment Detection Tailored to the Chinese Cyberspace

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing existing datasets (e.g., SWSR for online sexism detection) and analyzing platform-specific ecosystems (e.g., Xiaohongshu, Kuaishou) to classify and detect female competition rhetoric, body shaming, and gender confrontation using NLP text classification models.

Evaluating platform-specific public opinion data (e.g., Weibo, Toutiao) to identify regional discrimination, and proposing a multi-dimensional fine-grained annotation framework to label group-targeted prejudices based on regional characteristics.

Qualitative analysis of Chinese social media platform demographics and interactions (e.g., Kuaishou, WeChat Channels) to identify and categorize intergenerational confrontation and malicious teasing targeting the elderly.

Using active data manufacturing and large language model (LLM) prompt engineering to generate, annotate, and evaluate implicit derogation and systemic discrimination against specific occupational groups.

Applying interpretability tools (e.g., LIME, attention mechanism visualization, Integrated Gradients) to uncover spurious correlations, model vulnerabilities, and subjective human annotation biases that cause models to misclassify neutral terms or platform-specific jargon as toxic.
